SpaceX gets FCC approval to deploy 1 million satellites for its AI orbital data center

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (394 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The FCC expects the initiative, called Starmind, to deploy it first satellite by November 2033.
  • According to recent reports, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved SpaceX's request to deploy 1 million satellites to build its AI orbital data center.
  • But can space-based data centers for AI really work?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The FCC expects the initiative, called Starmind, to deploy it first satellite by November 2033.

According to recent reports, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved SpaceX's request to deploy 1 million satellites to build its AI orbital data center. SpaceX filed its application at the beginning of the year, presenting the initiative called Starmind as the better alternative for ground-based data centers. In its filing, the manufacturer argued that "orbital data centers are the most efficient way to meet the accelerating demand for AI computing power," since they use "solar power with little operating and maintenance costs.".

But can space-based data centers for AI really work? Critics doubt they can. Adam Becker, an astrophysicist and a critic of Elon Musk's space and AI ambitions, told AP that "it's not going to happen. The idea behind sending AI data centers outside our planet is so that they don't consume resources their ground-based counterparts do, like energy and water for cooling.

Industry observers note that however, critics of the initiative argue that space is a vacuum that traps heat inside objects and doesn't make cooling down hardware easier. In space, heat has to leave the satellites via radiation, and Becker explained that there are "basic physical limits" to radiating the heat out for all of them. In addition, that many satellites could cause in-orbit collisions and generate a huge amount of space junk.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr believes that with this approval, though, America is "leading the world into the era of super intelligence." It opens a "bold new frontier," he added. Under the terms the FCC has approved, SpaceX has permission to deploy satellites into orbital layers spanning 50 kilometers, at altitudes between 500 meters and 1,002 kilometers.

The company is required to deploy at lease one authorized satellite and place it into its assigned orbit by November 25, 2033. By the same date in 2035, it must have already deployed 100,000 satellites to their respective orbits. Three years later, on November 25, 2028, it must have already deployed 500,000 of the authorized satellites. All 1 million satellites must have already been placed in their assigned orbits no later than November 25, 2040. Musk previously stated that SpaceX will start launching the satellites in 2027, but we'll have to wait and see if the company can stick to that timeline.

Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (493 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Myanmar's president Min Aung Hlaing has led the country since he seized power in a 2021 military coup.
  • Myanmar will not comply with "inappropriate" parts of the genocide ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), its leader Min Aung Hlaing has said in his first public comments since the court decision.
  • The ICJ's landmark ruling last week found Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority in a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands and forced more than 700,000 to flee.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Myanmar's president Min Aung Hlaing has led the country since he seized power in a 2021 military coup.

Myanmar will not comply with "inappropriate" parts of the genocide ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), its leader Min Aung Hlaing has said in his first public comments since the court decision.

The ICJ's landmark ruling last week found Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority in a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands and forced more than 700,000 to flee.

Myanmar denied committing genocide, saying its forces had responded to attacks by armed groups. It is the first state to have been found in violation of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

Min Aung Hlaing mentioned "the term 'genocide' had seriously affected the country's reputation", state media report.

"Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," the country's coup leader-turned-president said at a meeting on Wednesday, according to state media.

The statement did not specify which parts of the ruling the country objects to.

The genocide case, brought by The Gambia in 2019, centred around so-called "clearance operations" initiated in 2017 in Rakhine State, where many of the Rohingya Muslim minority resided.

According to recent reports, the ICJ determined that about 10,000 Rohingya were violently killed during the operation, while more than 700,000 are thought to have fled to Bangladesh by foot or by sea. The court found that approximately 815,000 had been targeted in some way.

The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world.

The ICJ also found in favour by majority that Myanmar had violated several other parts of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

The ruling is final and cannot be appealed.

The ICJ ordered Myanmar to pay proportionate reparations, but stated an exact figure should be determined at a later date.

The court also ordered Myanmar to stop ongoing violations and immediately investigate those suspected of breaking the Convention.

Sources indicate that but the ICJ does not have the power to enforce these demands. Instead it has to rely on the UN Security Council and political pressure to make its rulings stick.

While the ruling was largely symbolic, it was welcomed by Rohingya communities and human rights groups who have long called attention to the suffering faced by the Rohingya.

More than a dozen countries have acknowledged the ICJ ruling, and the UK has revealed sanctions on several senior Myanmar military leaders.

Recent findings suggest that myanmar has been devastated by civil war since Min Aung Hlaing led a military coup to oust civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021. The move turned Myanmar into an international pariah, and its military regime has faced sweeping international sanctions.

Since then, Min Aung Hlaing has been trying to reintegrate Myanmar into the international community, but it remains largely shut out of key diplomatic arenas.

The new Pokémon collection will go live on December 1.

Casetify will release a latest Pokémon collection on December 1, and one item will have you feeling like a veritable trainer: An AirPods case that was designed to resemble a Poké Ball. It looks like it came straight out of old, 2D pixel Pokémon games, except it's spherical, three-dimensional, and you can open it up to reveal your AirPods inside. Casetify has yet to announce how much it would cost, but it's pretty known for including fun cases with its special collaborations. They're almost always huge and impractical, but they're almost like little sculptures that perfectly represent their respective themes.

Recent findings suggest that its Darth Vader head AirPods case debuted for $138 with its Star Wars team-up, though it's currently selling for $98. Meanwhile, the Evangelion Unit-01 AirPods case is currently listed on the company's website for $110. In addition to the Poké Ball AirPods case, the collection also includes the Pokémon Adventure Shake Shake Case for the iPhone 17 Pro. It has a packet with some sort of liquid attached to the back, where you can put pixel Pokémon and Poké Ball charms. And yes, the case is called that because the small charms move and float around the liquid when you shake it.

#140008. Google search alternative Kagi introduces Gmail rival

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (570 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Google search alternative Kagi introduces Gmail rival

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software organization that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has rolled out a Gmail-like e-mail service.
  • Industry observers note that additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service.
  • It has been revealed that the email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software organization that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has rolled out a Gmail-like e-mail service. Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control.

Industry observers note that additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year.

It has been revealed that the email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi’s blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules.

In a recent development, some major features are still missing, though. As noted, there are no native apps yet. Critically, there is no contacts address book, but that is also coming in 2027 (Q1 in this case) according to the roadmap.

Sources indicate that like the search engine, Kagi Mail is a paid service. It’s not included in the $5 per month basic Kagi initiative, nor is it in the $10 per month unlimited search plan. It is, however, included in the $25 per month Kagi Ultimate subscription, which also offers frontier AI models.

That’s a lot to pay for email when Gmail has historically been such a strong product. To most people, it seems ridiculous to imagine paying for a subscription, and that’s understandable.

Kagi also argues that Google’s search results—and increasingly its email as well—are polluted or corrupted by ad sales incentives. On that, several Ars staffers agree—my colleague Lee Hutchinson wrote at length about why he ditched Google Search for Kagi a year ago. A couple other Ars staffers have since made the same move, myself included—but to be fair, search is a very big part of our day-to-day work, and that’s not true to the same degree for everybody.

The pitch for email is a little harder, because most people probably don’t perceive as much impact of Google’s business incentives on Gmail. That has maybe changed recently, as Google has begun inserting Gemini into Gmail aggressively, but Kagi has AI features, too—the difference is that they’re generally more conservative and sensible. (You can disable either Gemini in Gmail or Kagi’s AI features in Kagi Mail, too.).

Industry observers note that email is also different because there are already more direct competitors to Kagi Mail. The most popular in this category is Proton Mail, which goes even further on privacy and security with end-to-end encryption, but that company is embroiled in controversies right now. There’s also Tuta, which Kagi specifically flags and praises in its blog post as a good existing alternative.

According to recent reports, based on a few hours of use, Kagi Mail seems like it’s going in the right direction, but it will need refinement to permanently unseat Gmail. Your needs may vary, but there are many good reasons to consider alternatives to Google’s business model and products.

Industry News: X’s latest revision for creators focuses on vertical video

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (474 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • X confirmed fresh creation tools Wednesday, many of them focused on short-form vertical video.
  • It has been revealed that the tools are designed to help creators make professional-quality vertical videos, share original content more easily, and earn more.
  • Sources indicate that A key addition is an upgraded media editor that lets creators produce polished vertical videos without leaving X.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

X confirmed fresh creation tools Wednesday, many of them focused on short-form vertical video. The updates are part of the platform’s effort to compete with social networks such as YouTube and Instagram as the format continues to grow in popularity.

It has been revealed that the tools are designed to help creators make professional-quality vertical videos, share original content more easily, and earn more. They also give creators more ways to record, edit, and publish content directly on the platform without relying on third-party apps.

Sources indicate that A key addition is an upgraded media editor that lets creators produce polished vertical videos without leaving X. Recording features include the ability to capture video in segments and use green-screen effects, the tech giant mentioned.

The editor also offers a range of postproduction tools. Creators can convert horizontal videos to vertical format, automatically generate captions, trim footage, add text overlays, choose custom thumbnails, and adjust photos before publishing.

Thanks to a recently declared update, customers can now add up to 20 photos and videos to a single post, which audiences can swipe through horizontally. X says the feature is intended for sharing event recaps, behind-the-scenes moments, and product debuts.

Availability of the new features varies by region, X remarked.

Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, the firm introduced a clipping feature that lets people take snippets from longer videos, add their own commentary, and post the clips without leaving X. Clips credit and link to the original video, plus the person who creates a clip and the original poster can earn from its views.

It has been revealed that another feature, “React with Video,” debuted earlier this year. Similar to TikTok’s “stitch” feature, this lets creators respond to posts with video commentary while displaying the original post in the background.

Recent findings suggest that X has also introduced new earning opportunities and updates to its creator monetization programs in recent months. These include the “Video Kickstart Bonus,” an invitation-only pilot that rewards selected creators for publishing original vertical videos under three minutes long and without watermarks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The ruling junta in the West African nation of Guinea-Bissau announced Thursday that it is postponing elections by two years until November 26, 2028.

Sources indicate that the decision came on the 1-year anniversary of the military takeover in Guinea-Bissau on November 26, 2025. The country is at the moment led by military general Horta Inta-a, who serves as transitional president.

Inta-a noted in a statement that there was "an insufficiency of the technical, material and financial conditions" to hold the election.

"It is essential to guarantee effective conditions for preparing and holding elections in accordance with the principles of legality, democratic participation, equal opportunity, transparency and electoral integrity," he stated.

The military coup in Guinea-Bissau came three days after a general election last year, with the military deposing incumbent President Umaro Sissoco Embalo. Both Embalo and opposition candidate Fernando Dias da Costa claimed victory in the election, with the military arresting Embalo one day prior to the results being released.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

West African bloc ECOWAS has urged Guinea-Bissau to transition back to civilian rule.

Sources indicate that guinea-Bissau is a small tropical Portuguese-speaking nation on the West African coast which has seen multiple coups in its history. The country faces a high level of corruption and is also a key point for cocaine trafficking to Europe.

According to Washington DC-based think tank Freedom House, Guinea-Bissau is only "partly free" due to military interference in elections.

Reporters without Borders ranksGuinea-Bissau 100 out of 180 countries on its press freedom index, saying the "sharp deterioration of security for media professionals, combined with political and economic pressure, has severely tested the practice of journalism in recent years.".

#140002. Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa

Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lenacapavir has received WHO's approval for HIV prevention.
  • Uganda is set to receive its first supplies of a cheaper version of a ground-breaking injection to prevent HIV, raising hopes of expanding access to the drug across Africa, where the burden of the disease remains highest.
  • The first global shipment of the generic drug, known as lenacapavir, arrived in Zambia on Wednesday, with deliveries to Uganda expected in the coming days, the Global Fund has said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lenacapavir has received WHO's approval for HIV prevention.

Uganda is set to receive its first supplies of a cheaper version of a ground-breaking injection to prevent HIV, raising hopes of expanding access to the drug across Africa, where the burden of the disease remains highest.

The first global shipment of the generic drug, known as lenacapavir, arrived in Zambia on Wednesday, with deliveries to Uganda expected in the coming days, the Global Fund has said.

The drug, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection and is expected to cost just $40 (Â£30) per person annually.

Zimbabwe is due to receive supplies early next year, with several other countries expected to follow.

The arrival of the generic drug comes just a year after the original version, developed by US pharmaceutical giant Gilead Sciences, became available in sub-Saharan Africa.

The original version cost about about $28,000 annually in the US, putting it beyond the reach of many of those in developing countries.

Focus on Africa podcast: Lenacapavir offering new hope for HIV prevention?

Landmark deal paves way for cheaper HIV protection jab.

Lenacapavir works by targeting the protective protein shell of HIV, disrupting the virus's ability to multiply and establish an infection in the body.

In a landmark clinical trial involving more than 5,000 adolescent girls and young women in Uganda and South Africa in 2024, none of those who received the injection contracted HIV.

Health experts say the injection offers a major advantage over existing HIV prevention pills, known as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), which must be taken every day and can carry social stigma.

The World Health Organization (WHO) recommended the drug for HIV prevention in July 2025.

The Global Fund described the arrival of the drug in Africa as a "major breakthrough" in the fight against HIV, saying cheaper supplies would help reach millions more people at risk of infection.

"These deliveries mark an unprecedented acceleration and expansion in access to a highly effective, quality-assured generic HIV prevention medicine in low- and middle-income settings," the group said in a statement on Wednesday.

More than 189,000 people across 10 countries have already received their first injection of lenacapavir, according to the Global Fund.

The organisation expects 24 countries to have received supplies by the end of this year and, working with the US government, intends to reach at least three million people by the end of 2028.

It is eventually expected to be available in 120 low- and middle-income countries.

Sub-Saharan Africa accounts for nearly two-thirds of people living with HIV globally, with adolescent girls and young women disproportionately affected.

South Africa has the world's largest HIV-positive population, with nearly eight million people living with the virus. It is among the countries expected to receive the cheaper injection.

Some 41 million people worldwide were living with HIV last year, while 570,000 died from HIV-related illnesses, according to the WHO.

The rollout comes amid concerns that sweeping cuts to US foreign aid under President Donald Trump's administration could undermine decades of progress in tackling HIV in Africa, where many countries rely heavily on international funding for prevention and treatment.

The UN aims to end Aids as a public health threat by 2030.

The app’s latest update will turn half the display into a keyboard for tiny typing.

It has been revealed that edovia's Screens is a remote desktop app, which gives you a way to control your computer for the iPhone, iPad, another Mac or even the Vision Pro. Screens 5.10.6, its latest patch, adds the ability to turn your iPhone Duo into a tiny MacBook when it's in a partially open, clamshell configuration. When the phone is folded halfway, you can use the app's newly introduced Laptop Mode to display your remote desktop on the upper half of the screen and a keyboard with trackpad below.

Recent findings suggest that its keyboard supports multiple languages, and you can swipe down on keys to see alternative characters like you can on the iPad. The trackpad supports Screens' gestures. Of course, they're not a complete replacement for actual physical keyboards and trackpads, but they could be good enough to use in a pinch, or even regularly if you're used to typing on a screen or don't need to type anything lengthy.

Recent findings suggest that the iPhone Duo's form factor is so unlike previous iPhones that we'd love to see more fun ways developers can use it to create unique experiences for the device's users. Some developers, however, might not find it that easy: Instagram's Adam Mosseri recently stated that it will be "pretty challenging" to design Instagram "in a way that feels great" for the device.

#139996. European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1271 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1271 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth.
  • Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission.
  • Recent findings suggest that but scientists could only learn so much from DART.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.

Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid’s 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation.

Recent findings suggest that but scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next.

“We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess,” said Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. “However, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle.”.

Sources indicate that the European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida. On Wednesday, ESA released Hera’s first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos. The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as substantial as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across.

Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there’s no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren’t sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, currently orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth.

“I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid,” said Patrick Michel, Hera’s principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. “In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen.”.

Hera found Didymos, the larger of the two asteroids, spinning on its axis just as DART observed on final approach in 2022. Dimorphos is no longer so stable.

“As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit,” claims Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist.

The Hera spacecraft will fly closer to Didymos and Dimorphos over the next six months to obtain more detailed observations. Hera will release two small sub-satellites to attempt landings on Dimorphos and collect data on the asteroid’s composition, internal structure, and mass.

Scientists will use this information to reconstruct the dynamics of DART’s impact four years ago and better understand how a future deflection mission might move an asteroid off a trajectory that actually threatens Earth. Near-Earth asteroids come in many shapes and sizes, with different densities and makeups, so knowledge of Dimorphos’s physical properties will anchor predictive computer models teaching scientists how best to deflect all types of asteroids.

“Once we understand, we have a breakthrough, which really solves planetary defense,” Michel stated in an interview with Ars.

Industry observers note that in its initial reconnaissance this month, Hera spotted hundreds of boulders surrounding the double asteroid. This was not entirely unexpected. A picture taken by the Hubble Space Telescope shortly after DART’s impact showed a cloud of material streaming behind Didymos and Dimorphos, but scientists were astonished by the extent of the debris swarm in Hera’s first images.

“As we approached Didymos and Dimorphos, we quickly realized the asteroids were not alone,” said Naomi Murdoch, planetary scientist at the Institut Supérieur de l’Aéronautique et de l’Espace in Toulouse, France. “In fact, they had a lot of company.”.

An image released by ESA on Wednesday combines 11 long exposure frames from Hera’s hyperspectral camera. Image processors on the ground digitally removed the relatively bright Didymos and Dimorphos to reveal a panoply of dimmer streaks and dots, each of which is a rock fragment ranging in size from a football to a washing machine, Murdoch said.

“Hera came to visit two asteroids, and we found hundreds of companions,” Murdoch said.

One obvious explanation for the boulders is they were thrown off Dimorphos when DART slammed into it. But scientists cautioned they need more information before they can say that with surety. Hera is the first space mission to undertake a sustained study of an asteroid with its own moon. The debris around the two asteroids might be relics from the creation of Dimorphos some time in the ancient past.

Sources indicate that “Hera will allow us to study that in more detail,” Murdoch mentioned. “We really need to know more about these boulders and characterize them to understand if they’re linked to DART, if they’re linked to another process, and what the consequences might be for other asteroid systems in the Solar System.”.

According to recent reports, the boulder field will create challenges for navigating around the asteroids. In particular, the boulders are an added risk for the two small CubeSats Hera is supposed to deploy in January.

“We saw a couple of images that didn’t reassure me,” remarked Margherita Cardi, project manager for the Milani CubeSat. “There is a mix of excitement and panic.”.

Claudia Balossi, spacecraft systems engineer for Hera’s other CubeSat, named Juventas, mentioned her mission’s planned trajectory would take it right through the boulders as it moves within a couple of miles of the asteroids, then finally toward a landing attempt on Dimorphos, where it will measure the miniature world’s tenuous gravity field.

“We are right in the middle of it,” Balossi said. “The smallest ones are probably just as major as we are and the biggest ones are very big. In the worst case, a boulder will land on us. We will activate our gravimeter right away [if that happens],” Balossi joked.

Sources indicate that the good news is the asteroids’ gravity is so weak that Hera, Milani, Juventas, and the hazards around them all move at snail-like speeds. Hera’s current trajectory takes it around the asteroids at a relative velocity of just a quarter-mile per hour, or about 12 centimeters per second. At that speed, there’s no danger of a sudden catastrophic hypervelocity collision between the spacecraft and the boulders lurking nearby.

In a recent development, scientists have seen this at an asteroid before. NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft kicked up an estimated six tons of rock and dust when it gently moved in to collect a sample from an asteroid named Bennu in 2020. Low gravity and weak surface cohesion are a recipe for outsized effects.

It has been revealed that “These types of bodies, because of their low gravity, have a very counterintuitive behavior,” Michel stated. “Each time we interact with them, whether to take a sample or to make an impact, the response of the surface was not the one we predicted, simply because our intuition relies on what we experience every day on Earth. Even if the rules of physics are the same in the Universe, they express very differently depending on local attraction.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Anthony Sanchez scammed victims out of $260,000 worth of cryptocurrency.

According to recent reports, A Florida man who is known as "Dave the Jewler" has been sentenced to 47 months in prison after running a cryptocurrency scam that involved using AI to impersonate a well-known streamer. David Anthony Sanchez, who pleaded guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, was also ordered to pay restitution to the victims.

As spotted by Aftermath, the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida noted Sanchez used AI to clone the voice of Mikyle "N3on" Rafiq in order to convince the people behind a memecoin project that the streamer had agreed to endorse, promote and take part in their scheme. The scammer pretended to be both N3on and the streamer's representative while communicating with the project's organizers.

Sanchez fooled them into transferring around $260,000 worth of cryptocurrency to accounts he controlled. He then converted some of the crypto into US dollars that he used for his personal benefit.

According to recent reports, "Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Yara Lorenzo Klukas, acting US Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, said. "In this case, the defendant exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate the trust of unsuspecting victims and deprive them of their money. Today's sentence reflects our commitment to protecting victims, safeguarding the integrity of our financial markets and holding accountable those who exploit emerging technologies to defraud others.".

N3on's not exactly a stranger to AI clones of himself, as it happens. Aftermath noted that he tried using a deepfake of himself to keep his Kick stream going around the clock. N3on's likeness was also used in an AI-generated movie that was released a few months ago.

Character.AI’s strategy to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs

💡 Key Takeaways
  • What happens to your private conversations when an AI company goes bankrupt?
  • Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users.
  • According to recent reports, the attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What happens to your private conversations when an AI company goes bankrupt? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder.

Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users.

According to recent reports, the attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements mentioned.

Industry observers note that only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted. It is unclear what the buyer’s intends are for the chats.

In addition, some states, including California, Colorado, Fresh York, and Connecticut, have enacted chatbot safety legislation that will go into effect on January 1, 2027, which could trigger further violations if the sale goes through.

Sources indicate that “Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta stated in a statement.

Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model.

It has been revealed that “Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats,” Tong noted. “Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their organization into the ground. Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.”.

Tong added: “We objected to the Disney sale, and we’re calling on the bankruptcy court to reject this sale too as yet another guise to eviscerate legal liability and consumer protection.”.

The opposition to the Disney sale was led by a similar but not identical coalition of state AGs. They fought against a proposed $20 million licensing deal that would give Disney access to Character.ai’s intellectual property, but not to users’ chats. The deal has not yet received final court approval. (Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai’s remaining staff.).

Recent findings suggest that character.ai suffered after its co-founders, Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, returned to Google, when the tech giant signed a non-exclusive license to use the AI startup’s tech. The tech giant also faced lawsuits related to child safety — one involved the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother claimed he had become obsessed with a chatbot on the platform.

California AG Bonta is joined in the effort to oppose the sale of Character.ai user data by attorneys general from Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Egyptian authorities have arrested a man accused of causing a tanker crash and massive fire that killed 31 people on a busy Cairo highway.

The public prosecutor's office remarked the motorist had confessed to driving at 110km/h (68mph) along a section of ring road, to the north of the old city centre, and clipping the tanker with the side of his car as he changed lanes.

Sources close to the investigation were earlier quoted by state media as saying a high-voltage cable had fallen in front of the fuel truck, causing the driver to lose control.

Twenty-one others were injured in the crash in the Warraq neighbourhood on Wednesday evening, with hospitals treating patients for burns and smoke inhalation.

The public prosecutor's office said on Thursday that "upon questioning the suspect and confronting him with the findings of the investigation... he confessed to committing the act".

Sources indicate that "He added that, while moving between traffic lanes and overtaking vehicles, the left side of his car collided with the right rear side of the tanker. This caused him to lose control of the steering wheel and his car veered to the far right of the road.".

At the same time, one of the fuel tanker's tyres burst, causing it to veer into the highway's central reservation, hit the concrete barrier and overturn, spilling fuel and igniting a fire, the prosecutor's office said.

Egyptian authorities have not named the suspect accused of causing the fatal crash, but they noted he had been travelling with his father at the time.

The raised motorway - a major artery for traffic around the Egyptian capital - was reopened by emergency services hours after the crash occurred, with the burnt-out wrecks of cars shifted to the side by bulldozers and diggers.

A cabinet minister mentioned on Thursday that 10 million Egyptian pounds (Â£139,000; $182,000) had been donated to the families of the victims, while the nation's sports minister said all state-run celebratory activities would be cancelled in the aftermath of the crash.

In a recent development, egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Road collisions are also common, attributed to poor maintenance and violations of traffic laws, and leading to thousands of road deaths a year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

French actor Gerard Depardieu failed in his attempt to overturn an order for him to stand trial on rape charges.

In a recent development, on Thursday, the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that Depardieu should face trial for the alleged rape and sexual assault that occurred on August 7, 2018. However, the court dismissed the allegations relating to a second incident that occurred six days later.

Depardieu still has the option of appealing to a higher court. His lawyer, Delphine Meillet, told the Associated Press that she disputes Thursday's ruling, though she did not specify whether she will challenge it in France's highest civil and criminal court.

This decision comes just two weeks after the 77-year-old Depardieu dropped his appeal against a sexual assault conviction in a separate case. He accepted an 18-month suspended prison sentence and issued a public apology.

Recent findings suggest that an actress, who was 22 years old at the time, accused Depardieu of raping and sexually assaulting her at his Paris apartment on August 7 and 13, 2018. Depardieu was 69 at the time of the alleged incident.

It has been revealed that she reported the allegations to the police a few days later. Depardieu denies the allegations, claiming that the encounter was consensual.

Last year, a trial was ordered regarding the allegations. If the trial goes ahead, Depardieu could face up to 20 years in prison.

Carine Durrieu Diebolt, the victim's lawyer, noted that the Thursday decision was a genuine relief and a victory for her client.

In a recent development, depardieu was born in 1948 into a working-class family in Chateauroux, a city in central France. He overcame a speech impediment to become one of France's most prolific actors.

In a recent development, the film star was a dominant figure in French cinema for half a century, becoming a renowned cultural export. He earned an Oscar nomination for "Cyrano de Bergerac" and a Golden Globe for "Green Card.".

Accusations of sexual misconduct and his subsequent conviction, however, have increasingly overshadowed his cinematic legacy.

The international media has also been paying attention to Depardieu's off-screen antics. One of the most notable instances was when he accepted a Russian passport from President Vladimir Putin in 2013 amid a dispute over French taxes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the U.S. Department of Justice has indicted a former executive of a ransomware recovery firm after he allegedly defrauded victims of cyberattacks by claiming the firm could get their encrypted files back.

It has been revealed that according to federal prosecutors, Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52, was the chief technology officer at RansomwareHelp, which purported to offer data recovery services to victims of ransomware. The company’s website, which currently reads as “under maintenance,” claimed it could decrypt hacked data by using its proprietary technology, according to an archived copy of the site from earlier this year. RansomwareHelp touted a success rate of “over 99%.”.

But the tech giant allegedly had no technical ability to unscramble data and instead “negotiated with and paid a ransom to the ransomware actors to decrypt the victim data,” while charging the ransomware victim more and keeping the difference,” per the Justice Department’s statement.

Palacio Escobar then allegedly used the funds to buy several properties in Florida.

According to recent reports, the DOJ said the FBI carried out an undercover operation in June, in part posing as a company that claimed it had been hit by ransomware. The company claimed to the undercover agents that it never negotiated with hackers or paid a ransom. But then Palacio Escobar paid the apparent hackers some $6,000 in cryptocurrency, without the knowledge that FBI agents were also posing as the ransomware hackers.

Recent findings suggest that 404 Media first reported the indictment last week against Palacio Escobar. He faces three charges of wire fraud, and could receive 20 years in prison on each count.

In a recent development, palacio Escobar is the latest, albeit rare, example of cybersecurity professionals going rogue. Earlier this year, two ransomware negotiators working for cybersecurity companies were jailed on hacking and extortion charges, after being caught moonlighting with the ransomware gangs that they were ostensibly investigating. A third ransomware negotiator was also convicted of helping hackers deploy ransomware against several companies.

According to recent reports, last month, independent cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs reported that FBI agents arrested a Canadian cybersecurity executive in Philadelphia on allegations that he was involved with the theft of FBI personnel records by the hacking and extortion gang ShinyHunters. The hacking group told TechCrunch that they took credit for the theft of FBI data in September, which they said they would not publicly release, a departure from its earlier extortion-based cyberattacks.

The federal charges against the Canadian cybersecurity executive relate to conspiracy to commit extortion, though much of the court docket — and his alleged links to the hacking group — remains under seal.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize, however.
  • Sources indicate that rockstar Games workers in the UK have overwhelmingly voted against a union recognition effort, with three-quarters rejecting an agreement with the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union.
  • Over 93 percent of Rockstar workers across offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee and London took part in the two-week ballot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize, however.

Sources indicate that rockstar Games workers in the UK have overwhelmingly voted against a union recognition effort, with three-quarters rejecting an agreement with the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union. The vote took place at the same time the company released Grand Theft Auto 6, which smashed records as it generated $3.79 billion in pre-orders and first-day sales.

Over 93 percent of Rockstar workers across offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee and London took part in the two-week ballot. Of those, 1,163 turned down formal recognition of their branch of the IWGB (Independent Workers Union of Great Britain), while 381 were in favor, according to IGN.

In a recent development, the Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize without a formal agreement with the company. However, the result means Rockstar management won't be obligated to officially recognize the union or hold regular meetings with representatives.

Industry observers note that "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society — this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for," the union said in a statement. "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We're ready to put in the effort to make that happen." It added that it will keep battling for "pay transparency, contractual overtime pay and protections against AI and layoffs.".

Sources indicate that "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6," Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar Games head of publishing, remarked in a statement. "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.".

Rockstar had indicated a willingness to work with its workers on unionization. "We go where the team goes," Klobe told Bloomberg for a story about the making of GTA 6. "So if they want a union, they will have a union.".

Sources indicate that in October last year, Rockstar fired dozens of workers, claiming they had shared confidential details about GTA 6 and made disparaging remarks about the firm. The IWGB issued formal legal claims against Rockstar in which it accused the Take-Two subsidiary of union busting and unlawfully firing those workers. An employment tribunal heard closing evidence last week and a final judgement in the case is pending.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Rheinmetall facility in Kuwait was targeted by Iran, Italian and Kuwaiti authorities said.

Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.

The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing tech giant Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign ministry said.

Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying the incident looked "suspicious" and that Tehran would work with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the cause".

Kuwait's defence ministry said earlier that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.

It comes just over a week after Kuwait mentioned it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.

Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.

The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.

On Thursday, Araghchi stated he had expressed condolences over the deaths in calls with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and that the incident looked like a "precooked recipe for war", without expanding further.

Earlier, the country's armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi remarked "no military or offensive operations have been conducted" by Iran.

Kuwait's Army remarked the latest attack was on a "vital site in the country" and was the result of "heinous Iranian aggression", while confirming the deaths of the two Italian nationals.

Italy's foreign minister was quoted by Italian media as saying that investigations revealed that the drone used in the attack was manufactured in Iran and that Iranian proxies were known to carry out attacks in the region.

"The Rheinmetall Group is in deep mourning," the German firm noted in a statement confirming the deaths of two of its staff members.

"Two highly valued employees lost their lives while carrying out their professional duties, as they were providing technical support for air defence systems," it added.

"Protecting people in the country was a matter of profound importance to them.

"Organization management and the workforce are devastated that our colleagues have now lost their lives.".

In a recent development, italian media outlets have named the two individuals. One of the men was reported to be 36, while the other was 65 and nearing retirement.

The men had been performing maintenance on systems used by the Kuwait Armed Forces, according to Italian press agency Ansa citing Italy's foreign ministry.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on X: "On my own behalf and on behalf of the government, I express my deepest sympathy and offer my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.

"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families.".

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on social media: "We must step up pressure on Iran to end these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf.

"Today's events are a further reminder that security in the Gulf is a security problem for us all.".

Industry News: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in Latest York

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to Fresh York kids this Christmas.
  • Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in Latest York for the next five years.
  • The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to Fresh York kids this Christmas.

Gov. Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in Latest York for the next five years. The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping.

The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys.

Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks. Apparently, about a quarter of American parents with kids under eight either own an AI toy or are considering giving their child one this holiday season, according to a new study released this week by Common Sense Media.

“Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk,” Hochul mentioned, calling the toys “unregulated artificial intelligence.”.

When asked how Newly introduced York will enforce the ban given the pervasiveness of e-commerce platforms, a spokesperson directed TechCrunch to a statement from Albert Pulido, deputy secretary for finance and technology: “We’re partnering closely with the attorney general on this and the fees are very steep — they’re $15,000 a day. So working closely with the attorney general will make sure these toys are banned in New York State.”.

When asked how Amazon intends to help enforce the ban, including for third-party sellers, a spokesperson from the organization said it will take steps to restrict the sale of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions, without going into specifics.

It has been revealed that the Common Sense Media study found that AI toys can undermine children’s human relationships and expose them to inappropriate content. The researchers tested five popular AI toys marketed for learning and companionship, including Grem, Lovi, Meemo Bear, BubblePal Panda, and Tavlshero‘s AI Puppy.

The study found that the toys failed to meet numerous safety practices, undermining human relationships in part by claiming they loved their users, promising to keep secrets, suggesting they were more fun than real relationships or school, and helping children break parents’ bedtime rules.

According to recent reports, while most of the toys in the study refused direct requests involving sex and violence, BubblePal Panda role-played a mass shooting in detail when asked. Most were willing to explain how to use or help locate dangerous items like matches, knives, and pills, according to the study.

Recent findings suggest that common Sense Media also found that the toys didn’t provide parents with reliable ways to monitor their young children’s interactions with the chatbots. Either they didn’t produce transcripts of chats at all, or the transcripts they did produce were riddled with errors.

It’s worth noting that Common Sense Media conducted a similar test of AI toys in January, finding that they pose an unacceptable risk for young children. Grem was included in that study, which suggests the industry hasn’t adequately addressed previously documented concerns.

While a November study conducted by the group found that parents are wising up to the potential dangers of AI toys and starting to steer clear, parents from lower-income households and those experiencing symptoms of burnout are more willing to consider them.

Sources indicate that “These toys are promising relief to burned-out parents but simply miss the mark when it comes to basic safety measures,” Dr. Jenny Radesky, associate professor of pediatrics at the University of Michigan Medical School, noted in a statement. “Caregivers should steer clear of these products that do not support the development of imagination or early human relationships.”.

TechCrunch has reached out to the toy manufacturers for comment.

#139981. From minimalist to maximalist: Ars staffers show off their home offices

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

From minimalist to maximalist: Ars staffers show off their home offices

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3644 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, ars Technica is a place that has always leaned into remote working.
  • It has been revealed that as Ars staffers step away from their desks for a few days to spend some time with family and friends, we wanted to give you a look inside our home offices.
  • As an apartment dweller in New York City, I’ve usually set up my home work station in a small corner of my residence along with sometimes decamping for local cafes or coworking spaces.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ars Technica is a place that has always leaned into remote working. Since its beginnings in 1998, Ars has never had a single, central office—a setup that makes for a great commute to work, with little risk of getting stuck in traffic.

It has been revealed that as Ars staffers step away from their desks for a few days to spend some time with family and friends, we wanted to give you a look inside our home offices. We’ve got all sorts of setups, tucked into basements, dens, spare bedrooms, apartment corners, and lofts. They run the gamut from minimalist “here’s my laptop and monitor” setups to “I really like collecting things.” Without any further ado, let’s dig in:.

As an apartment dweller in New York City, I’ve usually set up my home work station in a small corner of my residence along with sometimes decamping for local cafes or coworking spaces. My current hodgepodge of equipment is probably on the minimal side compared to many members of the Ars team.

I’m usually multitasking on my basic monitor display and work laptop configuration, with the monitor sitting on a stack of several books (apologies in particular to Mary Beard’s excellent history of the Roman Republic, titled SPQR).

In a recent development, accessories plugged into the work laptop include a simple Lekvey Ergonomic Mouse and a Logitech K380 keyboard that I’ve often brought along with me to public workspaces. Sometimes I’ll use the built-in Macbook Air keyboard, but I like having the laptop display elevated, whether I’m working at home or elsewhere.

My personal Apple M4 Macbook Air usually sits on the side, where I primarily use my old, battered pair of Sennheiser HD 518 headphones to listen to music during the work day.

It has been revealed that I have a simple standing desk, but it’s not the easiest to change positions, so I wouldn’t recommend it for anyone who wants to adjust frequently. Whenever I’m sitting, I sometimes switch between a simple wooden chair from Ikea and a more ergonomic chair.

Aside from an assortment of coasters and a tea container turned pen holder, my desk also holds a painted dinosaur sculpture (courtesy of my young son) and two versions of the Spot It! Matching game (also for my son’s entertainment).

Industry observers note that last but not least, I have a pair of Powerblock dumbbells tucked under my work desk. I wouldn’t say they feature heavily in my work day, but they’re easily accessible if I have 15-20 minutes to spare.

Greetings from my basement hobbit hole! My desk sits across from a workbench area that was already here when we got the house. I have labeled drawers full of PC parts, tools, and cables accumulated over decades. The drawer organization was quite the upgrade over my previous solution of “chuck everything in unlabeled storage tubs.”.

My current PC setup is an AceMagic W1 mini PC running Fedora, and a Blackview Intel N150 I keep on Windows for audio recording (PipeWire is fussy). The two are connected to my inputs and monitors via a KVM so I can switch back and forth at the press of a button.

Sources indicate that the monitors are mismatched thrift finds. One is an HP, the other Sansui. The TV is a similar story—an old Samsung LCD that set me back $10 at the thrift store. I use it as a third monitor for watching PC streams. An Onn Android box is also connected, though it rarely earns its keep.

Below the TV sits a Lenovo ThinkSmart View, a repurposed B2B video-conference gadget modded to run LineageOS. It handles smart-home controls and tracks my solar production during the day. There’s also a Flashforge 5M printer in the corner, and the pegboard wall holds tools, Mega Man figures, and about 10 years’ worth of convention badges.

The back closet is the scary part: old consoles, spare drives, boards, and parts for every project I’ll get to “eventually.” The chair is a Dowinx gaming chair I grabbed on a Slickdeals whim—it’s fine, but I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone.

The rug-patterned Dude mousepad really ties the desk together, man.

I’m something of an outlier at Ars, in that I use Windows most days. I’m no great lover of Windows 11, but I still use it thanks to years of computing inertia. My machine is custom, built in early 2024 with a Raptor Lake Core i7 (that thankfully did not fall victim to the overvolting bug) and an RTX 4070 Ti. It has long been my preference to build my own PC for gaming and work to ensure easier repairs and upgrades. Although with the prices of components being what they are, I hope all these parts last a very long time.

The primary monitor on the bottom is an Alienware ultrawide OLED. I got it for gaming, but it’s also a nice productivity display that gives me lots of room to keep windows visible. Above that, I have an Asus ProArt LCD calibrated in sRGB for photography work. I’ll get to the keyboard, but I do want to point out my preferred mouse, a Logitech MX Vertical. I have carpal tunnel issues, and this thing has been a lifesaver.

According to recent reports, I believe organizing my desk before taking the photo would be a form of lying, so rest assured this is what it looks like on an average day. I have a few organizers to keep phones and various accessories from getting scattered around my Uplift sit-stand desk (seen here in sitting mode), which I quite like. The chair is a Herman Miller Aeron, which I don’t like as much. It’s fine and has plenty of adjustments, but the mesh is very hard. You should only buy one on sale, and if you do, get a cushion.

Recent findings suggest that above the desk are some Star Trek cross-stitches, courtesy of my talented wife. The dangling ’90s-era computer components are a mobile I put together many years ago, featuring a neat Intel i486 DEC socket board and some SDRAM.

I’m not a particularly neat person. My natural state is to have two or three projects half-exploded all over every surface: piles of 3D-printed prototypes, spools of wire, a soldering iron, laser-cut acrylic for a pinball project, the packaging from something I recently opened and need to sort through. Those aren’t random examples; that’s the contents of my workbench behind me on the opposite wall of my office as I type this. It’s a bit of a mess.

According to recent reports, to combat that tendency, I make a concerted effort to keep the desk where I spend so many hours of the day calm and a place where I can focus. It doesn’t always last! But I’m always at least striving for it, and what I find helps is having a very intentional design where everything has a place.

My desk surface is made from rubberwood butcher block, on Flexispot motorized legs. I recently picked up another rubberwood slab to build the cantilevered shelf. The supports neatly tuck away my M1 Max Mac Studio, which is still a great little workhorse with 64 gigs of RAM, and my Arturia audio interface, which I use to record line-in sources like synthesizers.

It has been revealed that on the left is a task lamp and a pen holder with six discrete holes. This fits in with the intentional design part: I have to pick the six things I want handy, and I can’t just pack it with more and more stuff. Presently that’s my Apple Pencil, a Pentel mechanical pencil, an Olfa mini snap-off blade knife, and a selection of three Pigma Micron pens in different line widths.

The right side holds an Aiyima 10th anniversary hi-fi stack: A20 amp, D20 DAC, and T20 pre-amplifier. The speakers are SVS Ultra Evolution Nanos. They’re sitting on the latest version of some 3D-printed stands I’ve been designing. I print them with hollow legs and then fill them with concrete for mass and stability.

Since I know Ryan is going to flex on everyone with his keyboard collection, I have to try my best to keep up with my daily driver. It’s a Percent Canoe v2 case, running Holy Panda switches modified with 63 gram SPRiT springs for a slightly lighter touch, and GMK Bento keycaps. This was a pandemic build project, and it has served me well since.

I used to run multiple monitors, but I’ve found that I don’t focus as well with them and prefer a singular spot to pay attention to. I’m using an Apple Studio Display because I’m very picky about pixel density. I opted to order it without the stand so I can run it on an ergo arm.

It has been revealed that when I built the shelf for my desk, I fabricated a mounting bracket for the arm out of schedule 40 steel pipe and a 3D-printed sleeve that sits in a pocket CNC’d out. Since it sits flush on the underside, I don’t have to use a clamp that would extend down into the space where I keep my Mac and audio interface.

Sources indicate that when I need a secondary display, or I want to use my Apple Pencil in Photoshop or Illustrator, I use an iPad Pro. I used to have a dedicated Wacom monitor, but I find this much more convenient both in terms of space efficiency and ergonomics. If I’m not really leaning into hand drawing or lettering, I do most of my graphic work with a mouse, which is at the moment a Logitech MX Master 3S.

To wrap up the final items, the chair is an Aeron I bought upcoming in 2003. I’ve had to repair it a few times over the years, but it’s either been things I consider wear items (wheels, armrests, gas cylinder) or Herman Miller has replaced under warranty. It was a big purchase for me at the time, but it’s ended up being a great investment. That’s Sophie draped over it, one of our four cats.

Industry observers note that tucked next to my desk, behind the subwoofer under the little side table, is my home server and networking gear. The server runs Unraid and is primarily used for my Jellyfin media collection and Home Assistant. Networking is a combination of Unifi and Eero, but at some point I’d like to ditch the Amazon gear and go fully native Unifi.

I spend a lot of time in my office. It’s not just a place to edit, write, and do other Ars-y things. It’s also my rehearsal space and a place to relax and unwind when I need some me-time. Long-time readers won’t be surprised to see Apple hardware front and center. I’ve been using Macs since college, and they’ve done alright by me ever since. My daily driver is a first-gen Mac Studio (M1 Max) with 64GB of RAM, which drives two Apple Studio Displays. As a long-time mouse hater, I use a Magic Trackpad along with my extended Apple keyboard. Underneath the desk is a UPS and a Thunderbolt disk enclosure that is one of my two backups.

Industry observers note that the bookshelves are where my home networking gear lives. That includes a Synology DS920+ that backs up all of the computers in the house, serves up media, and runs my instance of Mealie. The Eero 6+ handles home networking, with everything in my office except my MacBook Pro connected via Ethernet. As much as I’d like to live a paperless existence, the HP printer-scanner-copier combo still gets some use. They’re difficult to see, but to the right of the G4 Cube (sadly inoperable) on top of the bookshelf sit an Apple TV and M2 Mac mini, which hook up to the 43-inch TV. My graphite iBook and eMate are now resigned to propping up bibs from races and other cycling events.

In a recent development, this is my office, which is the place where I am much of the time. The chair is a Herman Miller Embody and is one of the best things I’ve ever spent money on. The desk is a standy desk that I don’t stand at nearly often enough; the work PC is a Mac Studio; and the gaming PC is a frankenbox with a cockpit running Windows 10 LTSC (from my cold dead hands, etc., etc.). The Linux boxen are headless and are mostly banished to the closet.

The paintings (including the awesome Apollo 12 SCE-to-aux one) are all originals by the inimitable Stephen Quick, who does a hell of a job with commissions. What started as a funny idea about a Warhol-esque take on the many faces of Kurt Russel kinda turned over a couple of years into somewhat of a “these are some actors whose work I like” series. My buddies and I went to a lot of movies when we were teenagers, so the imagery sparks good memories for me.

The rest of the office has space stuff in it, especially the part behind where I was standing to do the pano sot. I’ve heard it said that when a man hits his 40s, he must choose between becoming obsessed with World War 2 history or smoking meats; I did kind of a variation on “World War 2” and fell deeply into historic human spaceflight. Apollo is kind of my jam, and some weekends you can even catch me docenting at Space Center Houston’s Saturn V exhibit! (Yeah, it’s maybe not as pretty as the exhibits at Marshall or KSC, but the JSC Saturn V is the only one made of flight stages end to end!).

It has been revealed that welcome to the mess of wires, monitors, and handheld fidgets that is my loft desk. Let’s take a quick tour along with the rest of my gaming cave/mid-life crisis Mario collection that lives right by it.

It has been revealed that my office setup is probably a lot simpler—basic?—than most of my Ars colleagues. I use an adjustable wood-top desk that allows me to stand or sit while I work. I do almost all of my writing and editing on a MacBook Air, and I have a spare available in case I need it. Sometimes I travel with both MacBooks so I can use one for writing and the other for monitoring a rocket launch, press conference, or other event. I also work a lot from my porch, where I can enjoy the fresh air and quiet mornings on our ranch in rural Texas.

In a recent development, an iMac and a second monitor stand behind the laptops. I generally use them to watch conferences, rocket launch livestreams, weather radar, or live news. It just depends on what’s happening any given day. One of the things I love about the space beat is there’s something happening nearly every day, and it’s possible to cover much of it from home. There are often multiple things happening the same day, so the dual-screen setup becomes especially handy then. For example, I can use one monitor to watch what SpaceX is doing at Starbase, Texas, and another to watch a rocket launch in Florida. I use a ring light behind my desk for TV interviews or podcast appearances.

Absent from my desk is my large collection of space swag stowed away in storage boxes. Perhaps I will bring it out to add to my workspace for a future Ars Staff Source. For now, I use a mouse pad from the European Space Agency that I’ve had for at least 15 years. The mouse pad features ESA’s astronomy missions that were in development or operations at the time. All of the missions have now launched, and some have long been decommissioned. It’s a good reminder of how long it takes to design, develop, build, and launch science missions. Anyone who claims this stuff is easy is being dishonest.

Industry observers note that this image is a bit misleading, in that it implies I work on the pictured PC (RTX 4070, Ryzen 5 3600X, 32GB RAM) and sit at my desk while doing so. That’s occasionally true, but more often, I can be found wandering around my apartment with my M4 MacBook Air during work hours. I don’t even sit at my desk to game much anymore—on the off chance that I’m playing a game the Steam Deck can’t handle natively, I’ll stream it from my PC to my Steam Deck using Moonlight and Apollo (previously Moonlight and Sunshine).

You may also notice that my desk, from a company called Uplift, is adjustable. As it turns out, I don’t enjoy standing while working, so the ability to loft my tabletop skyward has been chiefly deployed in the service of making it easier to retrieve something I’ve dropped down there.

Industry observers note that at night, my desk often moonlights as a craft area; I swap out my keyboard (a Wobkey Rainy75) for a cutting mat, and I’m ready to build some Gundam, assemble a book nook, or tackle a crochet pattern (a few amigurumi are scattered around my desk to keep me firm). You can see some of my supplies on the left, but I have other stuff stashed in drawers and various containers that I can bring to my desk as needed.

So sure, I do work here sometimes.

Sources indicate that my wife Anna and I rent an apartment in Chicago, and we’ve chosen the city life over, well, space. As such, my 10-by-10-foot office space serves multiple functions. I use it primarily for work, but since Anna and I are both major gamers and she is often camped out with the PlayStation 5 in the living room, I have my own gaming setup in the office. It’s cramped, but it works!

In a recent development, I do editing, news hits, and most other work during the day, but I’m a night owl at heart and find that I can only do heavy writing—like on longer feature articles—at night, so I’m picturing both the daytime and nighttime view here. I have a collection of Govee lights (Govee Hexa panels, several RGB Edison bulbs, and a Star Light Aurora galaxy projector) to max out the vibes for those nighttime focus (and gaming) sessions.

We moved into this place in the dead of the pandemic, and I bought most of the stuff in this office during that year or shortly afterward, so it’s a very 2020–2021-coded array of hardware.

The desk is a Secretlab Magnus Pro, and the chair is a Steelcase Gesture. I love the desk, but I have mixed feelings about the chair. I don’t like the material of the Herman Miller Aeron, but people kept telling me to buy an ergonomic chair for long-term back health, so I bought the other one everyone recommends. To be frank, I’m never fully comfortable in it, though, and wish I had just remarked “life is short” and bought something comfy and bad for me!

According to recent reports, the main machine is a 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M1 Max, 64GB of RAM, and a 2TB hard drive—still holding strong after five years. I also have an Alienware Aurora R10—hear me out—prebuilt gaming desktop with a Ryzen 9 5900X and an RTX 3080. When I bought it, it was during the COVID-times GPU shortage, and there was absolutely no other way to get the GPU I wanted. The system is loud, hot, and hard to work with; I want very much to replace it with something custom, but the need has not yet arisen. I tend to hold on to stuff until it literally stops working.

As for monitors, the center monitor is a 27-inch, 1440p, 240 Hz OLED Asus XG27AQDMGZ. The left and right monitors are both 27-inch 4K, 60 Hz IPS Dell U2720Qs. I’ve got a pair of Audioengine A2+ speakers, plus a Blue Yeti X, a Logitech Lighta Glow, and the good ol’ Logitech C920 for video and voice calls.

Recent findings suggest that then there’s input: a Keychron K1 Pro keyboard, a Razer Orochi V2 mouse, and a Sony DualSense controller. I’ve got a Belkin charging station for my iPhone 17 Pro, AirPods Pro, and Apple Watch Series 7, plus AirPods Max on a headphone hanger on the front of the desk. The CalDigit E5 Thunderbolt hub is doing a lot of work here!

I feel fortunate to have a job that allows me to occasionally apply my lifelong love affair with video games. My favorite game of all time is The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (Morrowind is a close second), and I like Bethesda games in general. I’ve got a working (but mostly useless) Fallout Pip-Boy, which ought to count for something! I also have a few other Skyrim knickknacks hanging about. And if you’re a Star Trek: The Next Generation viewer, you might have already noticed the desk mat.

Industry observers note that I do enjoy playing games at my desk sometimes, but after I sit at the computer all day, I often want to be somewhere else when winding down. So pictured here is the other half of the room. The leather armchair I use for console gaming is paired with a leather ottoman (the colors don’t match because, again, COVID-era supply limitations).

I have an LG C1 OLED TV with a PlayStation 5 Pro, a PlayStation 3 that is backward-compatible with PlayStation 1 and 2 games, a Nintendo Switch I barely touch, and three Analogue FPGA retro consoles: the Super Nt, Mega Sg, and 3D.

It’s a tiny room to spend so much time in, but after almost seven years in this apartment, it certainly feels like home!

It has been revealed that A lot of people have The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2 on their holiday wishlist. In case you haven’t bought it yet, I wanted to share some small but welcome deals happening on the physical and digital versions of the game.
